title: Console backend: rollout orchestration APIs + realtime stage status updates (ws/polling)
creator: Chloe Martin
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Context
- Dedicated staged rollouts introduces a stage state machine (progression, holds, approvals, rollback) with metric-based gates.
- Console needs a backend layer that:
  (1) exposes Console-friendly orchestration APIs (aggregated, permission-aware)
  (2) provides realtime-ish updates so operators can watch stage/gate evaluations without manual refresh

Problem
- Existing rollout APIs are control-plane oriented and return raw objects/events; Console requires a denormalized view (current stage, gate evaluation summaries, last evaluator tick, approval requirements, “why paused”).
- During dogfood we saw frequent page reloads and confusion about “stuck” states; we need a single source of truth for status and a consistent update channel (websocket with polling fallback).

Goals / Scope
1) Orchestration API surface for Console
- Provide a Console-optimized endpoint to fetch an aggregated rollout view:
  - stage list with weights, state, entered_at, pending_approval (who/what role), last_gate_eval_at
  - per-stage gate summary (pass/fail/unknown, failing gate name, last datapoint time, reason codes)
  - evaluator health hints (lag, missing metrics) and whether advancement is blocked by evaluator degradation
  - action availability (approve / abort / rollback / retry evaluation) computed server-side based on RBAC + rollout state
- Provide endpoints to page audit-ish events relevant to the Console (approvals, holds, auto-hold, abort), with stable ordering.

2) Realtime updates
- Implement a websocket channel (Console backend -> browser) that pushes rollout status updates when:
  - stage transitions
  - approval recorded
  - gate evaluation result changes
  - evaluator health changes that affects advancement
- Provide polling fallback with ETag / If-None-Match to avoid hammering the status endpoint.
- Ensure low-cardinality fanout: one subscription per (tenant, pool_id, rollout_id) per UI session; no per-request token dimensions.

Non-goals
- Implementing the control-plane state machine itself (handled in control-plane + evaluator work).
- Customer-facing self-serve; this is for operator + enterprise opt-in flows behind feature flag.

API Proposal (Console-facing)
- GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/status
  - returns aggregated status snapshot (see “Response contract” below)
- GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/events?cursor=…&limit=…
  - returns operator-relevant event stream (approval/hold/abort/auto actions) in descending time, cursor-based pagination
- WS: wss://console…/ws
  - subscribe message: {type:"subscribe", topic:"dedicated.rollout", pool_id, rollout_id}
  - push message: {type:"rollout.update", pool_id, rollout_id, version, payload: <same shape as status snapshot subset>}
  - heartbeat + server-side idle timeout; client auto-reconnect with backoff

Response contract (shape, not implementation details)
- rollout_id, pool_id, tenant_id
- plan_version (optimistic concurrency display)
- current_stage_id + current_stage_index
- overall_state: running | paused | holding | aborted | completed | rolling_back
- stages[]:
  - id, name, weight_percent, state
  - entered_at, last_updated_at
  - gates_summary: pass_count, fail_count, unknown_count, failing_gate_ids
  - block_reasons[]: e.g. NEEDS_APPROVAL, METRICS_STALE, EVALUATOR_LAG, CAPACITY_HEADROOM
- approvals:
  - required: true/false
  - roles_allowed[]
  - pending_since
  - last_approved_by + last_approved_at (if applicable)
- evaluator:
  - last_tick_at, status: healthy | degraded | down
  - metrics_freshness_seconds (computed)
- actions:
  - can_approve, can_abort, can_rollback, can_force_hold (operator only)
  - disabled_reason strings when false

Implementation notes
- Aggregation service:
  - Console backend will call control-plane RolloutPlan + Stage state endpoint(s) and evaluator summary endpoint (or read from the shared status aggregation endpoint once available).
  - Compute action availability and redaction based on RBAC claims (Kaitlyn + Marcus requirements).
- Realtime:
  - Prefer event-driven updates from the control plane (stage transitions / gate eval results) if available.
  - If event bus integration is delayed, use short polling internally (backend) and push diffs to connected clients (still better than every client polling).
  - Must be safe under partial failures: if websocket is down, polling still shows accurate state.

Acceptance Criteria
- Console can render rollout detail without additional ad-hoc calls to multiple services.
- Stage status on the page updates within ~5–10s of gate evaluation changes in typical conditions (best-effort).
- Polling fallback returns 304 with ETag when no status changes.
- RBAC enforced: users without approve permission do not see “Approve” enabled and do not see restricted event actor details (per security guidance).
- Load test sanity: 100 concurrent operator sessions watching rollouts across 20 pools does not materially increase control-plane QPS (target: < 1 rps per watched rollout from Console backend in steady state; ideally event-driven).

Open Questions
- Should the Console backend be the only websocket server, or should we use the existing unified “console-realtime” gateway? (Leaning: reuse existing gateway; this ticket implements handlers + topics.)
- Event ordering: if we mix evaluator updates + approvals, do we require strict ordering semantics or “last write wins” with versioning? Proposal: include monotonically increasing status_version from aggregation layer; client discards older payloads.

Links
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-staged-rollouts-prd
- Console UX spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-ux-staged-rollouts-dedicated
- Control plane architecture: confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/staged-rollouts-control-plane-architecture
- ADRs: adr-027 (gate evaluation) + adr-028 (approvals/audit)
- Related eng tickets: ENG-5122 (rollout endpoints), ENG-5124 (evaluator), ENG-5127 (console frontend)

Risk / Mitigations
- Risk: websocket fanout and frequent gate updates cause spiky CPU/memory.
  - Mitigation: throttle updates (coalesce within 2s), diff-only payloads optional, and per-connection subscription limits.
- Risk: missing metrics leads to flapping status.
  - Mitigation: explicit “unknown” + “metrics stale” reason codes surfaced consistently; no auto-advance.

Proposed Breakdown
- [x] Define Console status contract (backend + frontend alignment)
- [x] Implement status aggregation endpoint (snapshot)
- [x] Implement events endpoint w/ pagination
- [ ] Implement WS topic subscription + push updates
- [ ] Add ETag + polling fallback for snapshot
- [ ] Add integration tests: stage transition + approval + gate fail -> UI sees update
comments: 2025-01-16 (Chloe Martin): Creating as P0 because frontend work (ENG-5127/DES-133) needs a stable status contract and realtime story; current control-plane endpoints are too raw for Console.

2025-01-20 (Jada Williams): Drafted the status snapshot contract in the design doc. Key call: surface explicit block_reasons so we don’t need frontend heuristics for ‘why paused’. Also added evaluator health info to avoid ‘stuck’ confusion when evaluator lags.

2025-01-27 (Marcus Lin): Security review note: approvals/events must redact actor email for enterprise tenants unless user has audit.read scope. Make sure event payload includes actor_id and actor_type but only resolves display name when allowed.
2025-01-30 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): RBAC: action availability should be computed server-side. Frontend should not infer permissions from missing fields; return explicit booleans + disabled_reason.

2025-02-04 (Hannah Rivera): Implemented snapshot aggregation endpoint behind feature flag. Still missing ETag and WS push. Waiting on routing/state machine to finalize a couple of reason codes (CAPACITY_HEADROOM vs QUEUE_DEPTH).

2025-02-07 (Allison Grant): Observability ask: emit console_backend.rollout_status_fetch latency + cache hit ratio; and websocket subscribers gauge by topic. We’ll need this during beta to debug perceived UI staleness.

2025-02-11 (Rafael Mendes): During dogfood incident, operators were refreshing constantly. Please prioritize WS or at least backend-driven coalesced polling so clients don’t spike QPS during an incident.

2025-02-18 (Chloe Martin): Marking In Review. Snapshot + events endpoints are ready; WS topic handler implemented but needs perf validation. ETag support planned as follow-up if we can’t land before code freeze.
